threads.body:
The no-span path ignores `_attach_to_context`. When suppression is selected from an explicit `context` in a thread/task whose ambient context differs, entering the invocation never makes that supplied context current, so telemetry created by the underlying SDK is parented to the wrong trace (or becomes a root). Preserve the normal handler contract by attaching `ctx` when requested and detaching it when the suppressed invocation finishes.

This issue also appears on line 344 of the same file.

threads.body: An inference context only proves that one inference is an ancestor; it does not prove the new operation is duplicate instrumentation of the same model call. This branch suppresses every legitimate parent/child inference—including retries, fallbacks, or manually nested calls—and drops the child's span, event, and metrics. The previous parent/child test in `tests/test_utils.py` explicitly expected two nested inference spans and is changed in this PR to avoid this path. Deduplication needs an explicit/identity-based opt-in rather than triggering on any nested inference.

threads.body: A `LogRecordProcessor` receives an SDK wrapper (`LogData`/`ReadWriteLogRecord`), with the API `LogRecord` stored in its `log_record` field. Checking `event_name` directly on the wrapper therefore returns `None`, so the event is forwarded and this example does not suppress it. Inspect the wrapped record before forwarding.

+import os
+from typing import Any
+
+from openai import OpenAI
+
+# NOTE: OpenTelemetry Python Logs API is in beta
+from opentelemetry import _logs, trace
+from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc._log_exporter import (
+    OTLPLogExporter,
+)
+from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import (
+    OTLPSpanExporter,
+)
+from opentelemetry.instrumentation.genai.openai import OpenAIInstrumentor
+from opentelemetry.sdk._logs import LoggerProvider, LogRecordProcessor
+from opentelemetry.sdk._logs.export import BatchLogRecordProcessor
+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
+
+
+class DropGenAiEventsProcessor(LogRecordProcessor):
+    """LogRecordProcessor wrapper that suppresses GenAI inference operation details events.
+
+    This processor filters out the ``gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details`` event:
+    1. Early drop: ``enabled()`` returns ``False`` when checking the event name,
+       allowing the SDK and instrumentation to avoid constructing the event payload.
+    2. Fallback: ``on_emit()`` drops the record if it is emitted.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, processor: LogRecordProcessor) -> None:
+        self._processor = processor
+
+    def enabled(self, *, event_name: str | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> bool:
+        if event_name == "gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details":
+            return False
+        if hasattr(self._processor, "enabled"):
+            return self._processor.enabled(event_name=event_name, **kwargs)
+        return True
+
+    def on_emit(self, log_record: Any) -> None:
+        if (
+            getattr(log_record, "event_name", None)
+            == "gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details"
+        ):
+            return
+        self._processor.on_emit(log_record)

Split the deduplication implementation, tests, fixture changes, and changelog into a dedicated PR so this feature can be reviewed and released independently.

threads.body: `InferenceData` is now exported as public API even though repository production code does not consume it outside the private implementation. This creates a long-term compatibility commitment for an internal mutable transport type without a documented user-facing contract. Keep it private unless external instrumentations genuinely need to construct it; if they do, document and test that supported contract explicitly.

This snippet uses `Any` in method annotations but never imports it, so copying the documented example raises `NameError` while defining the class. Include the typing import in the code block.

This issue also appears in the following locations of the same file:
- line 38
- line 55

@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+Suppressing Inference Events Programmatically
+=============================================
+
+This example demonstrates how to suppress ``gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details``
+log events programmatically in Python by wrapping an OpenTelemetry
+``LogRecordProcessor``.
+
+Overview
+--------
+
+When capturing content with ``EVENT_ONLY`` or ``SPAN_AND_EVENT``,
+the OpenTelemetry GenAI instrumentation emits a
+``gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details`` log event containing input/output
+messages and metadata.
+
+If you want to collect spans and traces while selectively dropping the inference
+event without disabling logging globally, you can wrap your log record processor
+with a custom processor:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+    from opentelemetry.sdk._logs import LogRecordProcessor
